families.source: UKHSA Legionnaires' disease clinical, microbiological and epidemiological case definitions
families.topic: confirmed and probable cases, exposure categories, clusters and outbreaks
evidence_points: A confirmed Legionnaires' disease case requires pneumonia plus specified laboratory evidence.
Accepted laboratory evidence includes culture, Legionella pneumophila urinary antigen or Legionella nucleic acid detection in a lower respiratory specimen.
A probable case definition applies only after an outbreak has been declared.
Exposure assessment generally considers the 2 to 10 days before symptom onset.
Healthcare-associated exposure categories distinguish overnight stays, employment and visits.
Cluster definitions vary for healthcare, travel-associated and community exposures.
An outbreak includes 2 or more linked cases with onset dates connected within 28 days and additional microbiological or strong epidemiological evidence.
Enhanced surveillance data supports application of the national case definitions.
Geographical proximity or a shared venue alone does not confirm a common Legionella source.
A case can remain assigned to more than one potential cluster until microbiological or epidemiological evidence identifies or excludes a source.

families.source: UKHSA public health control and management of diphtheria in England
families.topic: case investigation, close-contact management, treatment, vaccination and outbreak control
families.page_title: Diphtheria: public health control and management in England
evidence_points: The guidelines cover investigation and management of diphtheria cases and close contacts in England.
They are intended for UKHSA health protection teams and NHS staff involved in diphtheria control.
The publication includes 2025 public-health control and management guidance.
Supplementary guidance addresses cases and outbreaks in asylum seeker accommodation settings.
The guidance incorporates antibiotic susceptibility testing and management considerations.
Clearance swab requirements form part of case and carriage management.
Immunisation assessment is a core element of diphtheria prevention and control.
The publication includes principles for managing macrolide-resistant infections and setting-specific outbreaks.
Detection of a Corynebacterium species alone does not establish toxigenic diphtheria.
Case classification and contact action require specialist laboratory evidence, vaccination history and UKHSA risk assessment.

families.source: UKHSA national pertussis public health management guidance
families.topic: pertussis cases, contacts, outbreaks, testing, surveillance and communication
families.page_title: Pertussis: guidelines for public health management
evidence_points: The publication provides national guidance on public-health management of pertussis.
It is intended for health protection teams and partners managing cases, contacts and outbreaks.
The scope includes healthcare and educational settings.
The page includes current guidance updated in May 2026.
It provides supporting material on pertussis testing in primary care.
It includes surveillance forms for outbreaks in healthcare settings.
It includes surveillance material for severe or fatal paediatric pertussis.
Template communications are provided for parents, healthcare services and exposed healthcare workers.
A clinical suspicion or contact history alone does not determine the complete public-health response.
Management requires current case timing, age, vaccination, exposure, testing and vulnerable-contact evidence.

families.source: UKHSA administration guidance for HNIG measles post-exposure prophylaxis
families.topic: HNIG eligibility, timing, administration, dosage and storage for measles exposure
families.page_title: Administration of HNIG for measles post-exposure prophylaxis
evidence_points: The guidance applies to England and addresses human normal immunoglobulin for measles post-exposure prophylaxis.
HNIG can be used to attenuate measles in eligible susceptible immunocompetent infants and pregnant women.
The publication addresses products manufactured for subcutaneous administration.
It explains that available products may be administered intramuscularly or subcutaneously in the specified context.
Urgency of measles post-exposure prophylaxis is a reason for practical community or outpatient administration.
The page includes explicit timing considerations for HNIG administration.
It includes dosage, storage and further-information sections.
The guidance was updated on 16 July 2026.
Exposure alone does not establish HNIG eligibility; susceptibility, risk group and timing must be assessed.
HNIG guidance does not replace national measles case management, vaccination assessment or specialist clinical advice.
